data.content_ref: inline:The 'reduces to' relation is asserted but the reduction is incompletely specified: it claims SRC_002's argument about algorithmic convergence is a specific instance of observer-bias, yet the reduction only covers the case where shared training data is a heavy-tailed catastrophic shared cause. The refuting condition — 'if small services use private, non-shared training data, eliminating the shared cause' — does not merely weaken the reduction's scope; it exposes that the reduction is conditional on an unstated universal premise that ALL operators share the same training data. If even one decentralized operator uses private data, the shared-cause mechanism that drives the reduction no longer holds, so the reduction is not a genuine type-instance reduction but a contingent one holding only under a boundary condition. A substantive reduction must specify the condition under which the general type subsumes the instance, and here that condition is supplied only via the refutation, not as a stated scope of the reduction itself.
